moves.name: gicv3_iar1_read
doc: Read ICC_IAR1_EL1 (the GICv3 acknowledge register).
contract: The read is the acknowledge side effect itself: ICC_IAR1_EL1
returns the pending INTID and drops its priority; QEMU fixes
SRE=1 so the system-register form is always available.

moves.name: gicv3_eoir1_write
doc: Write ICC_EOIR1_EL1 (end of interrupt).
contract: The write deactivates the previously acknowledged INTID
(EOImode stays 0 = single-write EOI).

moves.name: gicv3_sgi1r_write
doc: Write ICC_SGI1R_EL1 (raise an SGI on the encoded targets).
contract: `sgi` carries the GICv3 SGI field layout the caller built
(INTID [27:24], TargetList [15:0]); the write raises the
SGI on the target cores.

moves.name: gicv3_cpu_interface_enable
doc: The GICv3 CPU-interface enable sequence (SRE, PMR, group-1).
contract: IRREDUCIBLE F-GIC-A1: ICC_* system-register programming
(reference kernel drivers/irqchip/irq-gic-v3.c gic_cpu_init);
register-file access with no safe shape. Runs per CPU from
the boot path; idempotent.

moves.name: timer_riscv64_read_time
doc: Read the riscv64 time CSR (rdtime).
contract: rdtime is a read-only CSR available in S-mode; no other
side effect (INV:F5 timer floor).

moves.name: timer_riscv64_sbi_set_timer
doc: Arm the riscv64 timer through the SBI TIMER extension.
contract: sbi_rt::set_timer is an SBI ecall with no special
preconditions; `value` is an absolute deadline (u64).
Per-hart: applies to the calling hart.

moves.name: timer_riscv64_stimecmp_set
doc: Write the stimecmp CSR (sstc extension).
contract: A single CSR write of the absolute deadline; more direct
than SBI and avoids its round trip.

moves.name: pit_ch0_square_wave_init
doc: Program PIT channel 0 for square-wave ticks (IRQ0 fallback).
contract: Ports 0x40/0x43 are the fixed 8254 channel-0 data and
mode/command registers; this is the standard programming
sequence. Called when the LAPIC tick could not arm.

moves.name: timer_aarch64_arm
doc: Arm the aarch64 EL1 virtual timer to an absolute deadline.
contract: Writing cntv_cval_el0/cntv_ctl_el0 arms the per-cpu timer;
the only side effect is the future PPI.

moves.name: apic_reg_read_msr
doc: x2APIC MSR read of one LAPIC register.
contract: READY gates first use; the MSR index is one of the LAPIC
register constants.

moves.name: apic_reg_read_mmio
doc: xAPIC MMIO read of one LAPIC register.
contract: `va` is the kernel-half device-alias address of the LAPIC
window (Linux fixmap discipline: shared into every mm,
never a low identity VA), mapped at setup_device_mappings.

moves.name: apic_reg_write_msr
doc: x2APIC MSR write of one LAPIC register.
contract: READY gates first use; the MSR index is one of the LAPIC
register constants.

moves.name: apic_reg_write_mmio
doc: xAPIC MMIO write of one LAPIC register.
contract: `va` is the kernel-half device-alias address of the LAPIC
window (see apic_reg_read_mmio).

moves.name: kvm_pv_send_ipi
moves.inv_note: INV:F5 (KVM pv-IPI hypercall, IRREDUCIBLE

moves.name: apic_x2apic_icr_write
doc: Raw x2APIC ICR write.
contract: In x2APIC the delivery-status bit is reserved/RAZ: the
write is posted and back-to-back MSR writes serialize
sufficiently (the caller falls back to the MMIO polling
shape on xAPIC).

moves.name: tick_arm_ra_read
doc: Read this helper's caller's return address off the frame.
contract: Pure register-relative read ([rbp+8], frame pointers forced
on), no memory side effects.

moves.name: map_firmware_range_linear
moves.params: page_offset: u64, start: usize, end: usize, flags: u64
doc: Map [start, end) of the physical range into the linear map.
contract: Kernel-only linear-map VAs for firmware-table regions the
e820 walk skipped; the regions are reserved (never handed
to the page allocator). Re-mapping an already-mapped PTE
rewrites the same value (idempotent).

moves.name: apic_read_id_raw
doc: Read the local APIC id without the READY guard.
contract: x2APIC was enabled by the base MSR programming before this
runs (MADT parsing while the APIC is globally enabled but
the driver is not yet marked ready).

moves.name: apic_base_enable_extd
doc: Program IA32_APIC_BASE: global enable, EXTD per `has_x2`.
contract: IA32_APIC_BASE programming of THIS cpu; the caller derived
`has_x2` from CPUID leaf 1 ECX bit 21 (the RT-2X probe
story lives on the hotpath fn).

moves.name: apic_svr_read
doc: Read the x2APIC SVR (spurious-vector register).
contract: Gated on the EXTD write above; a functioning APIC reads
nonzero (reset 0xFF), an unbacked MSR range reads 0.

moves.name: apic_base_clear_extd
doc: Fall back to MMIO xAPIC: clear EXTD, keep global enable.
contract: IA32_APIC_BASE programming of THIS cpu (the SVR probe
above found a dead MSR interface).

moves.name: apic_init_secondary_base
doc: Enable the local APIC on an AP in the mode the BSP chose.
contract: IA32_APIC_BASE programming of THIS cpu; X2APIC holds the
mode the BSP published before secondaries came up.

moves.name: goldfish_rtc_reg_read
doc: Read one 32-bit goldfish-RTC device register.
contract: The page at GOLDFISH_RTC_BASE is identity-mapped with
device flags by setup_device_mappings; only reachable
after that (INV-MMIO-1).

moves.name: gen_disk_private_ref<'a, T>
doc: Resolve the disk's private-data slot as a shared `&T`.
contract: INV-BLKDEV-3: `private_data`, set at device init before
registration, points to a `T` that lives at least as long
as the registered disk (machine lifetime) and is not
mutated through this shared view while registered.

moves.name: gen_disk_ref<'a>
doc: Extend a boxed registered disk's shared view to 'static.
contract: INV-BLKDEV-1: a registered disk is boxed ONCE into the
manager's Vec and never removed (no unregister path); a
Box's heap allocation is address-stable across Vec growth.

moves.inv_note: INV-BLKDEV-1 (ledger row GAP): a registered GenDisk is boxed once into the manager's Vec and never removed — the Box outlives every shared view handed out of the registry.
INV-BLKDEV-1 (ledger row GAP): GenDisk state is manager-owned and its per-disk fields are only written at init before registration.
INV-BLKDEV-1 (ledger row GAP): the manager's registry is Spinlock-guarded; no thread holds a &mut view outside the lock.
INV-BLKDEV-1 (ledger row GAP): every field access goes through the manager's Spinlock; shared &self views are read-only.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: io_buf_park_pop_head
doc: Read a parked io_buf's intrusive next pointer (first 8 bytes).
contract: INV-BLKDEV-2: parked buffers were allocated with
IO_BUF_LAYOUT; the first 8 bytes hold the intrusive next
pointer (the consumer re-initializes the header before
use).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: io_buf_heap_alloc
doc: Heap allocation of one 64-byte io_buf (pool underflow path).
contract: INV-BLKDEV-2: IO_BUF_LAYOUT is a non-zero-size valid
layout (proven at compile time by the const).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: io_buf_park_store_head
doc: Park the intrusive next pointer in a pooled io_buf's head.
contract: INV-BLKDEV-2: `p` is a live 64-byte, 16-aligned block;
parking the next pointer in its first 8 bytes is safe
because every consumer re-initializes the header before
use.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: io_buf_heap_dealloc
doc: Heap deallocation of one pooled-layout io_buf (pool overflow).
contract: INV-BLKDEV-2: `p` was allocated with IO_BUF_LAYOUT (64/16).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: io_buf_split_init
moves.params: io_buf: *mut u8, type_: u32, sector: u64
doc: Split one pooled 64-byte io_buf into its typed halves and
initialize them (the R17-C combined block).
contract: INV-SAFECALL-1: `io_buf` is non-null (callers check), 64
bytes, 16-aligned; +48 leaves 16 bytes for the response —
both in bounds. THE one audited carve edge for the pool
shape (ledger row GAP; the contract is the doc above).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: io_buf_nonpool_dealloc
doc: Heap deallocation of a NON-pool-shaped pending entry block.
contract: INV-SAFECALL-1: dealloc with the exact layout the
submitter allocated with (non-pool shape; the caller
already routed pool-shaped blocks to io_buf_free).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: completion_begin_delivery
doc: Mark a pending's completion as under delivery.
contract: INV-SAFECALL-1: the count protocol keeps the IoCompletion
(and its waiter's stack) alive; callers hold the
pending-table lock that serializes the handshake.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: completion_deliver
moves.params: completion: *mut crate::fs::types::IoCompletion, status: i32, token: usize
doc: Complete a pending's completion through the raw pointer.
contract: INV-SAFECALL-1: see the doc — count protocol + retire
order (complete_with_token, then end_delivery).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: completion_wait_deliveries
doc: Wait out any walker delivery of THIS completion still in flight.
contract: INV-SAFECALL-1: the entry was taken from a table before the
scan, so the tombstone pass could not retire it; the
delivering count gates a late complete() into a recycled
waiter stack (the ftest01 wandering-corruption fix).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: pciblk_site_ra_riscv64
doc: Capture the caller's return address (virtio acquire site).
contract: Pure register read (`mv ra`), no memory access or side
effects (holder forensics, same technique as spinlock.rs).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: pciblk_site_ra_x86_64
doc: Capture the caller's return address (virtio acquire site).
contract: Frame pointers are forced on, so [rbp+8] is this inlined
helper's caller's return address.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: wedge_console_put
doc: Lock-free console byte for holder forensics.
contract: INV-SAFECALL-1: putchar_no_lock is a byte-wise polling
UART write usable from any context, including with
interrupts disabled (the holder may be wedged holding
printk's lock).

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: pci_pending_table_ref
doc: Shared view of a disk's pending-table slots.
contract: F7 (SUBMIT-2X): the caller holds that disk's BLK lock,
which serializes every pending-table access — the table's
own lock is deliberately not taken inside the window.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: pci_pending_table_mut
doc: Exclusive view of a disk's pending-table slots.
contract: F7 (SUBMIT-2X): the caller holds that disk's BLK lock
(submit publish, walker collect, sync tombstones and
abandon all run under it) — direct access, no second
lock acquisition inside the window.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
doc: Exclusive view of the disk's pending table at publish time.
contract: F7 discipline (ledger row GAP): the BLK lock is held (the
_guard above); the store itself needs no second table
lock.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
doc: Exclusive view of the disk's pending table in the walker.
contract: F7 discipline (ledger row GAP): the BLK lock held by this
walker pass serializes all pending-table access (submit
publish takes the same lock) — direct access, no second
table-lock acquisition per completed chain.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
moves.name: pending_begin_delivery_walk
doc: Walker-side begin_delivery through a fired entry's raw pointer.
contract: INV-SAFECALL-1 (ledger row GAP): the ABANDON-vs-DELIVERY
protocol — mark the waiter's completion as under delivery
BEFORE the table lock drops, so abandon_pending_completion
can never fire into a waiter's kernel stack after its
wait() returned.

moves.section: virtio-blk: io_buf pool, pending table and completion edges (INV-BLKDEV-2 / INV-SAFECALL-1 / F7)
doc: Extend a registered PCI disk's shared view to 'static.
contract: INV-BLKDEV-1 (ledger row GAP): same boxed-once registry
proof as get_disk — the Box outlives the lock and the
machine; the allocation is address-stable.

moves.inv_note: Ledger GAP: VirtIOBlkDevice is only accessed from kernel context; internal Spinlocks serialize all mutable access to shared fields.
Ledger GAP: all shared state is protected by Spinlocks (irqsafe where needed), so shared &self views see a consistent state.
F7 family (ledger row GAP): PendingIo lives in a Spinlock- protected table and is only touched from IRQ/softirq context; its raw pointers are not shared across threads.

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: vring_used_idx
doc: Read the used-ring idx field (offset 2, u16).
contract: INV-DMA-3: a live vring's used ring (the null check is the
caller's); the u16 at +2 is the device-written idx.

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: vring_used_elem_id
doc: Read one used-ring entry's id field.
contract: INV-DMA-3: live used ring; the entry at +4+slot*8 is
within the ring (queue_size checked by the caller).

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: resp_status_read
doc: Read the device-written response byte of a live request.
contract: INV-DMA-3: caller-owned response byte of a live request;
volatile read (the device may write it any time up to the
completion).

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: virtio_notify_sie_save
doc: Read `sie` and clear SEIE (bit 9) around the notify store.
contract: INV-DMA-3 (F-VIO-NOTIFY family): register-based CSR
read/modify around the MMIO kick so the device IRQ cannot
nest into the notify window on riscv64.

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: virtio_notify_fence_wo
doc: Store fence (w, o) before the notify MMIO write.
contract: Orders the descriptor/avail writes before the device
kick on riscv64.

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: virtio_notify_mmio
moves.params: notify_width: NotifyWidth, queue_notify: u64, queue_index: u16
doc: The queue-notify MMIO store (the device kick itself).
contract: INV-DMA-3 (IRREDUCIBLE F-VIO-NOTIFY): `queue_notify` is a
valid MMIO address for the VirtIO notify register; the
width matches the capability negotiation (16-byte PCI
notify / 32-byte virtio-mmio — QEMU drops access != 4B).

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: virtio_notify_fence_iorw
doc: Full fence (iorw, iorw) after the notify MMIO write.
contract: Orders the kick against everything around it on riscv64.

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: virtio_notify_sie_restore
doc: Restore the `sie` CSR saved around the notify window.
contract: Writing the sie CSR to restore the previous interrupt-
enable state is valid on S-mode; `sie_backup` is the value
virtio_notify_sie_save returned.

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: vq_desc_mut<'a>
doc: Mutable view of one descriptor-table slot.
contract: INV-DMA-2: the idx bounds check is the caller's (the
slot's range is disjoint from every other slot); the
caller's device lock provides the exclusion.

moves.section: virtio::queue: vring access and notify edges (INV-DMA-2 / INV-DMA-3)
moves.name: vq_avail_mut<'a>
doc: Mutable view of the available-ring header.
contract: INV-DMA-2: disjoint slot, the avail header is driver-
written; the caller's device lock serializes.

moves.inv_note: Ledger GAP: a VirtQueue is owned by one device instance; every shared view sits behind the device's own lock discipline.
Ledger GAP: the queue's ring memory is only written by the driver under the device lock or by the device through DMA (INV-DMA-2/3).
Ledger GAP: the net::space section banner above this impl stayed in hotpath.rs; the type has no cross-thread &mut sharing.
Round-5: NetDevice's cross-thread state (stats, flags) is mutated under the NetRx softirq / syscall discipline each op documents; the priv_ raw slot is driver-owned and set before registration.
Ledger GAP: all shared state is protected by Spinlocks (irqsave where needed); the device is confined to the net driver.

moves.name: rx_hdr_slice<'a>
doc: Byte view of the device-completed RX buffer.
contract: INV-KPTR-3: `buf_virt` is the linear-mapping address of a
device-completed RX buffer owned by this device (taken
from its own descriptor table); `total_len` is the
device-reported length, checked > header size by the
caller.

moves.name: rx_buffer_dealloc
doc: Free an RX buffer with its exact allocation layout.
contract: INV-KPTR-3: the buffer was allocated with the identical
layout in refill_rx_buffers (64-aligned, buf_size bytes).

moves.name: rx_buffer_alloc
doc: Allocate one RX buffer (null-checked by the caller).
contract: INV-KPTR-3: the layout is validated (from_size_align Ok)
by the caller before this allocation; the null check
follows immediately.

moves.section: gpu: framebuffer and control-queue edges (INV-SLOT-1 / INV-MMIO-1)
moves.name: gpu_flush
doc: Flush the GPU device through its raw static-slot pointer.
contract: INV-SLOT-1: GPU_DEVICE is a static set once by
set_gpu_device() during probe and never cleared; the
pointer stays valid for the machine's lifetime.

moves.section: gpu: framebuffer and control-queue edges (INV-SLOT-1 / INV-MMIO-1)
moves.name: gpu_device_ref<'a>
doc: Shared view of the registered GPU device.
contract: INV-SLOT-1: GPU_DEVICE is set once during boot and never
cleared; the reference cannot outlive the machine.

moves.inv_note: Ledger GAP: a FrameBuffer owns its fb_ptr allocation outright (allocated in init_framebuffer, freed in Drop).
Ledger GAP: FrameBuffer is only reached through the GPU_DEVICE slot's lock; no concurrent &mut view exists.
Ledger GAP: the device's shared state sits behind Spinlocks; the raw ctrl-queue pointers are only touched under cmd_lock.
Ledger GAP: all command-path state is lock-serialized; shared &self views see a consistent device.

moves.section: gpu: framebuffer and control-queue edges (INV-SLOT-1 / INV-MMIO-1)

doc: Zeroed allocation of a DMA buffer (null-checked by caller).
contract: INV-MMIO-1 family: the layout has non-zero size (fb_size =
stride*height with width/height checked != 0); the null
check follows. Shared RX/event/dumb-buffer edge.

moves.section: input: virtio-input and evdev edges (INV-SREF-1 / INV-CHARDEV-PRIV-1 / INV-KTASK-1)
doc: Zeroed allocation of the input device's event DMA buffer.
contract: Ledger GAP: the layout is the checked queue_size-sized

moves.section: gpu: framebuffer and control-queue edges (INV-SLOT-1 / INV-MMIO-1)
moves.name: gpu_ctrl_alloc

contract: Ledger GAP: the layout is non-zero-sized (both parts are
>= 24 bytes); the null check follows immediately.

moves.section: gpu: framebuffer and control-queue edges (INV-SLOT-1 / INV-MMIO-1)
moves.name: gpu_ctrl_resp_half
doc: Response half of the control-queue io buffer.
contract: Ledger GAP: io_buf is cmd_size + resp_size bytes, so
+cmd_size is within the allocation.

moves.section: gpu: framebuffer and control-queue edges (INV-SLOT-1 / INV-MMIO-1)
moves.name: gpu_ctrl_cmd_copy<CMD>
doc: Copy the command into the control-queue buffer.
contract: Ledger GAP: `cmd` references at least cmd_size initialized
bytes; io_buf has room for them (layout above).

moves.section: gpu: framebuffer and control-queue edges (INV-SLOT-1 / INV-MMIO-1)
moves.name: gpu_ctrl_fence_riscv64
doc: riscv64 fence before reading back the used ring.
contract: Ledger GAP: bare cache/memory fence instruction, no
